sca.title: SCA Standard 310-2021 Home Coffee Brewers: Specifications and Test Methods
quotes: In this standard, brew ratio is expressed in grams of coffee per 1.000 kg of fresh water at 17±3°C (g/kg).
The brew ratio used for testing in this standard: 55 g of coffee per 1.000 kg of water.
shall reach a temperature in the 90 to 96°C range by the moment when 33% of the water mass has been sprayed
The temperature shall be maintained within the 90 to 96°C range for the remainder of the brew cycle.
Target extraction parameters shall be a brew strength of 1.15-1.55% at the standard brew ratio.

https://www.aboutcoffee.org/brewing/drip: Coffee-to-water ratio: 1 to 2 tablespoons of ground coffee for every 6 ounces of water (the “Golden Ratio”)
https://www.aboutcoffee.org/brewing/pour: Coffee-to-water ratio: 1 gram of coffee to 13-16 grams of water (1:13 to 1:16)
https://www.aboutcoffee.org/brewing/fren: Coffee-to-water ratio: 1 gram of coffee to 10–16 grams of water (1:10 to 1:16)
https://www.aboutcoffee.org/brewing/cold: Coffee-to-water ratio: 1 gram of coffee to 4-5 grams of water (1:4 to 1:5)
Let the coffee sit and steep in the refrigerator or at room temperature for 12 hours, or overnight.
https://www.aboutcoffee.org/brewing/espr: Coffee-to-water ratio: 1 gram of dry coffee to 2 grams of brewed espresso (1:2), where 1 is the weight of dry coffee grounds and 2 is the weight of liquid espresso extracted
